text:
olivia: quick design check — thinking about splitting the single \"Approve\" action in the evals UI into two tiers: a fast
'quick approve' for low-risk passes and a 'formal approve' that creates an audit entry and requires confirmation. Feels like it maps to real workflows at customers who have reviewers vs. sign-off engineers.

sam: curious — what's the main goal? reduce accidental full approvals or give explicit auditability?

olivia: both. pattern we see: PMs want speed for obvious passes, security/compliance needs a traceable event for audits. Right now one button does both and copy is ambiguous.

tara: from infra side — if we add an audit variant we need an event emitted with approver id + prompt-set snapshot. low cost but needs schema bump. also we should avoid blocking fast flows.

lee: a11y concerns: adding multiple approve buttons can confuse screen reader users if we don't group and label them clearly. propose clear aria-labels and role=\"group\" with legend, plus distinct confirmation dialogs (aria-modal + focus trap).

mike: did some intercept interviews — reviewers often want a visible indicator of the \"trust\" level used to approve. they liked the idea of two verbs because it matches their org language.

olivia: mock attached (link) — layout idea: stack primary actions as a split control, with a subtle divider and a tooltip explaining audit implications. copy proposals inside.

olivia: proposed copy (quick draft):
```
Primary button: Approve (fast)
Secondary: Approve and record audit
Tooltip on secondary: Create an immutable audit record with approver and snapshot
Confirmation modal title (formal): Approve and create audit entry
Modal body: This will mark N tests as approved and create an audit record. This action is recorded and cannot be undone.
Buttons: [Cancel] [Approve and record audit]
```

sam: copy feels direct. prefer shorter button text to reduce visual weight — maybe \"Approve\" and \"Approve + Audit\"?

olivia: ok to shorten: \"Approve\" / \"Approve + Audit\" — keeping tooltip for clarity.

lee: accessibility nit: buttons should include aria-describedby linking to the tooltip content, and we should not rely only on hover. tooltips must be focusable or announced. also keyboard shortcuts?

tara: we could add keyboard shortcuts: Mod+Enter = Approve, Mod+Shift+Enter = Approve + Audit. Implementation: frontend mapping + capture in telemetry. low risk.

mike: make sure we test discoverability — in user interviews people didn't hit shortcuts unless exposed in the confirmation and a short hint near the button.

olivia: agree. show hint under primary: \"Press ⌘⏎ for quick approve, ⇧⌘⏎ for audit\" (hide for screen readers, provide separate sr-only text).

lee: for screen readers: provide an sr-only line like: \"Quick approve — will mark tests as passed. Approve and record audit — will also create an audit entry that is permanent.\" and use aria-live to announce the result after approval. ensure the result panel receives focus.

tara: backend event payload: {approver_id, timestamp, mode: \"fast\"|\"audit\", prompt_set_sha, changed_tests: []}. nothing crazy. we should version event name: evals.approval.v2.

sam: rollout plan idea: behind feature flag per-org. default to existing single-approve for small orgs, enable new modal & audit for enterprise customers gradually. track mistakes (undone approvals) and time-to-approve as metrics.

olivia: UX QA checklist for this change:
- focus order: toolbar -> primary approve -> secondary approve -> modal focus in confirm
- screen reader: both button descriptions announced, modal announces consequences
- keyboard: both shortcuts work, tab order preserved
- visual: buttons meet contrast and spacing tokens
- bulk flows: bulk approve modal shows count and domain summary (no read of 1000 items)
- tooltip: accessible alternative for SR users

lee: add one more: if a user triggers Approve + Audit, surface the audit id in a small toast with a link to the audit entry (toast must be role=\"status\" and keyboard dismissable).

mike: for usability testing: 5 users for discoverability + 5 for bulk workflow. include 2 screen reader participants. plan next week.

tara: dev tasks: frontend PR for split button + shortcuts, api contract change, backend event emission, feature flag gating, toggle in admin. estimate ~3 dev days + 1 day QA.

olivia: design tasks: update mocks, annotate a11y callouts, prepare microcopy variants.

sam: decision: proceed with split-approve design behind flag, use short copy \"Approve\" / \"Approve + Audit\". add keyboard shortcuts and sr-only descriptions. roll out to beta orgs first.

olivia: cool. action items: @tara open infra ticket with event schema (assign to me for copy) — due EOD Thursday. @lee add a11y checklist to the PR template. @mike schedule the usability sessions. I'll update the figma and share link.

notify-bot: Created issue #4527: \"e(VALS) split-approve + audit event\" and assigned to tara.

sam: thanks everyone — if no objections I'll file the product spec today and link the figma to the ticket.

olivia: no objections from my side. :thumbsup:

lee: no objections. small note: include aria-role in the spec.

tara: ack. starting a branch tomorrow.

mike: scheduling invites now.

olivia: end — will post updated mocks once branch is up.
